senses.gloss: m. (cucuma, κουκκούμιον, prob. of Semitic origin; the form cucumus is not recorded in Lat. Dict.) kettle (smaller than מיחם).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 3:7">Kel. III, 7</cite> <he>קומקום</he> Mish. ed. (Talm. ed. <cite ref="S00405"><he>קומקומוס</he></cite>; Maim. <cite ref="S00405"><he>קומקומס</he></cite>). Ib. XIV, 1 <cite ref="S00405"><he>קומקום</he></cite> (ed. Dehr. <cite ref="S00407"><he>קומקמוס</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Tosefta Mikvaot 7:1">Tosef. Mikv. VII</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Mikvaot 8:1">VIII</cite>), 1 <he>קומקומים</he> ed. Zuck. (corr. acc.; oth. ed. <cite ref="S00405"><he>קומקום</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 6:1:7">Y. Pes. VI, 33ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>כבק׳ הזה אני יורד לו</he> (not <he>בק׳</he>) I would meet him as if attacking him with a (boiling) kettle; <he>מה הק׳ הזה וכ׳</he> as a kettle scalds and wounds and blackens (if thrown at a person), so would I &c.; <cite ref="Menachot 109b:18">Men. 109ᵇ</cite> <he>אני מטיל עליו ק׳ וכ׳</he> I would throw a kettle of hot water at him.

<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 2">Deut. R. s. 2</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 517:4">Yalk. Hos. 517</cite> <cite ref="S00407"><he>קוּמְקְמִין</he></cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <he>קוּמְקוֹמוֹסִין</he>, <cite ref="S00407"><he>קוּמְקְמוֹ׳</he></cite>, <cite ref="S00407"><he>קוּמְקְמִין</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 75b">Ab. Zar. 75ᵇ</cite>; Y. ib. V, end, 45ᵇ; <cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 158">Sifré Num. 158</cite> <he>קוּמְקְמָסִים</he>; Tanḥ. Ḥuck. 2 <he>קוּנְקוֹמוֹסִין</he> (ed. Bub. <he>קומקמסין</he>).
